A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIOTM and retain matching methods, theory, and core experiments. The complete documents, including Appendices A–C in v1 and A–D in v3, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 report original synthetic transport, image-translation, and regularization experiments, with additional generated examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds alignment, time-sampling, cycle-consistency, and high-dimensional benchmark results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The bidirectional transport maps, displacement-interpolation objective, HJB regularizer, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Separate parameter subscripts clarify notation; alternative samplers are tested as ablations without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds the continuous neural OT benchmark on Gaussian mixtures in dimensions 16 and 64, extending direct transport-map evaluation beyond v1's two-dimensional examples. Existing synthetic datasets and CelebA/AFHQ translation coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table 7 introduces comparisons with L, QC, MM, MMv1, MMv2, MMv2:R, and MM-B, explicitly using baseline scores from Korotin et al. (2021). This substantially broadens the reported comparator set; the original comparisons in Tables 1–3 are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds LPIPS evaluation, round-trip reconstruction MSE using two directional OTM models, Beta time-sampling experiments, and L2-UVP/cosine evaluation with a separate 100K-iteration configuration. These are new protocols; the expanded FID sample-count description clarifies existing evaluation rather than establishing a changed setting.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to uniform versus Beta time sampling, approximate inversion of the learned maps, and preservation of source-image properties. Figures 12–14 additionally compare qualitative behavior across regularization strengths and track FID throughout training, extending v1's endpoint sensitivity and loss-curve analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new test-set mean LPIPS scores do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original figures retain their results, while Tables 4–7 add substantial numerical evidence. New sampler FIDs are 11.85 and 12.45 versus uniform sampling's retained 10.72; DIOTM wins four of six cycle tests and reports L2-UVP of 2.5% and 10.4% at dimensions 16 and 64. Figures 12–14 add qualitative comparisons and FID trajectories.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly states the almost-sure inverse identities T2 composed with T1 equals the identity, and conversely, as the cyclical property. The central duality and HJB theorems and Appendix A proofs are otherwise retained; continuity made explicit in the main theorem was already used in v1's proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and central conclusion retain the same claims about displacement interpolation, the HJB regularizer, improved stability, and transport accuracy. The added experiments support or qualify those claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion explicitly identifies restriction to quadratic costs as a limitation. Appendix D adds interpretations of weaker cycle-reconstruction results and non-leading high-dimensional performance, including a proposed accuracy/scalability tradeoff involving ICNN constraints.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 specifies approximately 500 source test images, 5000 generated/reference samples for Wild-to-Cat, and 12247 samples for CelebA FID. Appendix D.3 documents the added benchmark's optimizer and MLP architecture, while Table 2 clarifies result provenance. These extend the existing implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Wasserstein barycenters, flow matching, ICNNs, LPIPS, and the continuous OT benchmark, and discusses positioning against constrained transport solvers. Section 4's broader research narrative remains largely unchanged; the additional Kolesov entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify barycenter connections, intermediate-distribution matching, parameter notation, and evaluation details. v3 adds acknowledgements and Appendix D while retaining the main section sequence and most existing prose and proofs.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables, two substantial qualitative comparison grids, and training-trajectory plots as Figures 12–14. Existing Appendix C image grids are redistributed across pages without changing their content, and Table 2 gains a provenance explanation.

improvement.justification: The added alignment, cycle, sampler, and higher-dimensional tests make DIOTM's behavior and limitations easier to assess, while explicit FID sample counts improve reproducibility. These are useful extensions of the retained empirical case. A new reporting inconsistency limits the polish: Appendix D.1 names lambda=50 as OTM's successful Male-to-Female setting, whereas Figure 14(b) and Section 5.2 indicate lambda=10.
